Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Jhamman Ram-Ist, learned Aga for the State apprised the Court that he has received
instructions in the present matter, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be
disposed of on merit.
2. Heard Sri Satish Trivedi, learned senior Advocate assisted by Sri Ajay Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jhamman Ram-Ist, learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 387 of 2023, under Sections 420, 466, 467, 468, 471, 409 IPC, Police Station Sadar Bazar,
District Saharanpur, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and according to the FIR applicant was posted in the Court of C.J.M. Saharanpur as Senior Clerk and he was custodian of the record and Rohitash Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196063040/

sentences.text: 1 record of number of cases of C.J.M. Court were found in the office of RPF Saharanpur.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and applicant never committed either alleged offence or the negligence.

He further submits that, however, applicant was posted in the Court of C.J.M. Saharanpur as Senior Clerk but at the time of the alleged incident he was looking the protocol work of the District on the direction of the C.J.M. concerned.

He further submits that as the FIR of the present case was lodged after the order of District Judge concerned, therefore, applicant had to file the instant anticipatory bail directly to this Court and after considering the entire facts of the case this Court on 25.09.2023 entertained his anticipatory bail application and released the applicant on interim anticipatory bail.

6. He further submits that now charge-sheet has been filed and applicant fully cooperated with the investigation and as during investigation applicant was duly protected, therefore, after submission of the charge-sheet applicant may be enlarged on anticipatory till conclusion of the trial.
He further submits that after submission of charge-sheet in the present matter the custodial interrogation does not appear to be necessary.

He further submits, however, apart from the present case applicant is also having a criminal history of another case but FIR of that case was also lodged along with the FIR of the present case and in that case applicant is also on interim anticipatory bail.
He further submitted that applicant is having apprehension that if he will appear before the court concerned then he will be sent to jail.

7. Per contra, learned A.G.A opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail and submitted that applicant was the Senior Clerk in the court of C.J.M and he misused his possession and the record of the number of cases were found in the office of the RPF and being custodian applicant cannot be skip from his liability but he could not dispute the fact that after considering the entire facts of the case this Court on 25.09.2023 released the applicant on interim anticipatory bail and now charge-sheet has been filed.
He further does not dispute that fact that after submission of the charge-sheet the custodial interrogation does not appear to be necessary.
8. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. From the record, it reflect that FIR of the present case was lodged by the order of the District Judge concerned and according to the FIR the applicant was senior clerk in the Court of C.J.M.
Saharanpur and due to his misconduct the record of the cases were found in the RPF office, but contention raised by learned counsel for the applicant that at the time of incident he was looking the protocol work of the C.J.M. and he was not the custodian of the record cannot be ruled out.

Further,
from the record it reflects that after considering the entire facts of the case this Court released the applicant on interim anticipatory bail on 25.09.2023 and he did not misuse the liberty of bail granted to him and in the meantime charge-sheet has been filed.
The custodial interrogation in the present matter does not appear to be necessary.
10. Further, apprehension of custody/ arrest raised by applicant cannot be completely brushed aside.

However, from the record it appears that apart from the present case applicant is also having criminal history of one another case but FIR of that case was also lodged on the same date i.e. on the Rohitash Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196063040/
2 date when the FIR of the present case was lodged and in that case also applicant is on interim anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: 11. Therefore, considering the facts of circumstances of the case discussed above the the interim anticipatory bail granted by this Court vide order dated 25.09.0223, is hereby confirmed and applicant shall continue to remain on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

15. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
